_doc: SM302 convention: the mechanical half of this review's findings, so the next review re-runs the SAME check rather than reinventing it. Prose stays in the dimension files. `verify` exits 0 when the finding is FIXED, run from the repository root. A finding without `verify` is reported as not-mechanical.

findings.title: a dying service is counted, backed off and FAILED (the reap is the exit event)
findings.verify: grep -q 'service failed - not restarting' lib/Lazysite/Daemon/Supervisor.pm && test -f t/unit/daemon/06-a-dying-service-is-counted-backed-off-and-failed.t

findings.title: the enabled gate is re-read while the supervisor runs
a job account that does not exist is refused as such, via account_names
the daemon reads its config through the manager's plugin-conf reader, not a fourth parser
one shared atomic JSON writer in Lazysite::Util
a test starts the supervisor with the plugin enabled
the Hestia README states the per-instance memory cost
an idle tick does not rewrite the run record
one supervisor per docroot (a lock) and orphan adoption
findings.verify: grep -q 'sub _acquire_lock' lib/Lazysite/Daemon/Supervisor.pm && grep -q 'stopping an orphaned service' lib/Lazysite/Daemon/Supervisor.pm

findings.title: status requires the recorded kernel start time, not the pid alone
stopping children has a deadline then KILL
a torn run record is logged
the daemon has run on a real host and the run is recorded
SECURITY.md has a significant-change entry for the daemon
performance.md no longer says there is no daemon
findings.verify: ! grep -q 'No$' docs/architecture/performance.md || ! grep -q 'daemon, no process manager, no listening socket owned by lazysite' docs/architecture/performance.md

findings.title: DEVELOPER.md names the runtime and how a job is added
an ADR records the runtime's decisions
lazysite-common ships a postinst that reloads systemd
